name: github
description: GitHub connector: read-only access to an organization's or a user's repositories, commits, pull requests, issues, releases and code.

listing.summary: Read repositories, commits, pull requests and issues on GitHub, read-only.

credentialFields.name: token
credentialFields.label: GitHub fine-grained personal access token (read-only: Contents, Metadata, Pull requests, Issues)

setupGuide.summary: Connect a GitHub organization or user read-only with a fine-grained personal access token. Liaison refuses a token that can write.

steps.text: On github.com, open your avatar → **Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens** and choose **Generate new token**.
Under **Resource owner**, pick the organization (or yourself), and under **Repository access** the repositories Liaison may read.

Under **Repository permissions**, set **Contents**, **Metadata**, **Pull requests** and **Issues** to **Read-only**. Leave everything else at No access: never Read and write, never Administration. A classic token with the `repo` scope can write and is refused.
Set the longest expiry your organization allows. An expired token answers 401 and every GitHub read stops until you paste a new one.
Copy the `github_pat_…` value and paste it into the **token** field.
In **owner**, enter the organization or user name exactly as in its GitHub URL (e.g. `maison-example`).
Rotating later: come back to this same form and paste the new token. It REPLACES the stored credential rather than adding a second connection.

sections.title: Connection
sections.description: Read-only connector for a GitHub organization or user: repositories, commits, pull requests, issues, releases.

agentInstructions: GitHub connector provides read-only access to the connected GitHub organization or user. Call github_list_repos first to discover repositories. Tools are read-only — no write operations. When GitHub is not connected, surface a not_connected error, do not fabricate data.
